property_summary: For any caller other than the current owner, transferOwnership must not change the owner state variable; the buggy version violates this by allowing any caller to change owner.
After transferOwnership is called, the owner should be the newOwner; the buggy version keeps the original owner.

For any address newOwner, after a successful call to transferOwnership(newOwner) by the current owner, the owner() getter must return newOwner; the buggy version leaves owner unchanged, violating this property.
After any call to transferOwnership, the owner should be the newOwner argument; the bug always sets it to address(0) regardless of input.
For any non-zero address call to transferOwnership where the caller is the current owner, the owner must change to the newOwner argument; the bug always sets it to address(0) regardless of input.
For any initial owner and new owner address, after a non-owner calls transferOwnership, the owner of C must remain unchanged; the buggy modifier allows anyone to change the owner.
For any initial owner and any non-owner caller, a call to transferOwnership must revert and leave the owner unchanged; the buggy version allows the non-owner to succeed and change the owner.
For any caller who is not the current owner, a call to transferOwnership must revert; the buggy version allows a non-owner to succeed.

For any non-zero initial owner and any other address newOwner, after a non-owner calls transferOwnership(newOwner), the owner must remain the initial owner; the buggy modifier allows a non-owner to set owner to newOwner.
For any initial owner and any non-owner caller, transferring ownership via transferOwnership must only succeed when the caller is the current owner; the buggy version allows any caller to succeed.
A call to owned() must revert when called by a non-owner. The mutant makes it succeed for everyone, violating the onlyOwner access control.
A call to owned() should succeed when called by the current owner. The buggy version makes it always revert, so it reverts even for the legitimate owner.
For any caller, owned() succeeds if and only if caller is the owner. The reference contract enforces this; the buggy modifier removes the check, so owned() succeeds for any caller.
After any non-owner calls transferOwnership, the owner state variable must remain unchanged; the buggy version allows any caller to change it.
